records.source: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־פְּנֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ עָלָ֖יו וַיִּשַּׁק־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And fell Joseph on [the] face of his father, and he wept over him and kissed him.
pieces: Joseph flung himself down on his father's face, kissing him and weeping over him.

L.1: And Joseph fell on his father's face and wept over him and kissed him.

R.1: Joseph bent down and put his face against his father's face. He cried over him and kissed him.

decisions.reason: God had promised Jacob that Joseph's own hand would close his eyes (46:4). Joseph, who wept when he met his brothers and his father again (45:14-15; 46:29), weeps now at the parting.

records.source: וַיְצַ֨ו יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶת־עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶת־הָרֹ֣פְאִ֔ים לַחֲנֹ֖ט אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וַיַּחַנְט֥וּ הָרֹפְאִ֖ים אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And commanded Joseph his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and embalmed the physicians Israel.
pieces: Joseph instructed the physicians who served him to embalm his father, and so the physicians embalmed Israel.

L.2: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.

R.2: Joseph had doctors who worked for him. He told them to embalm his father's body, and so the doctors embalmed Israel.

decisions.choice: embalm: preserve the body, Egyptian custom
decisions.reason: Egyptians preserved the bodies of the dead with spices and drying salts. It was not an Israelite custom; here it kept Jacob's body for the long journey to Canaan. Only Jacob and Joseph (verse 26) are said to have been embalmed in the Bible.

decisions.choice: his servants the physicians: doctors in his service
decisions.reason: Eved here describes the physicians as men who served Joseph, a high official; it does not say whether they were slaves.

decisions.choice: who served him / who worked for him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the physicians' position without calling them slaves (meaning decision m2).

records.source: וַיִּמְלְאוּ־לוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י הַחֲנֻטִ֑ים וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ מִצְרַ֖יִם שִׁבְעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And were fulfilled for him forty days, for thus are fulfilled [the] days of the embalming; and wept for him Egypt seventy days.
pieces: Forty days were needed for this, since embalming takes that long, and the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.

L.3: And forty days were fulfilled for him, for so are fulfilled the days of embalming. And the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.

R.3: It took forty days, because that is how long embalming takes. The Egyptians mourned for him for seventy days.

decisions.reason: The Greek historian Herodotus also describes the Egyptian embalming process as taking about seventy days in all. Egypt's mourning for Jacob is close to the honor given to a king.
The name of the land stands for its people.
English says the people, not the country, wept.

records.source: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י בְכִית֔וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶל־בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם דַּבְּרוּ־נָ֕א בְּאָזְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And passed [the] days of his weeping, and spoke Joseph to [the] house of Pharaoh, saying, if, please, I have found favor in your eyes, speak, please, in [the] ears of Pharaoh, saying,
pieces: Once the days of weeping for him had passed, Joseph addressed the household of Pharaoh: "If you look on me with favor, please speak for me in Pharaoh's hearing and tell him:

L.4: And when the days of weeping for him had passed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

R.4: After the time for mourning ended, Joseph went to Pharaoh's officials. He said, "If you are willing to help me, please give Pharaoh this message from me:

decisions.reason: The text does not say why Joseph, Pharaoh's highest official, asks others to speak for him. He may still have been in mourning dress, unfit to appear before the king, or he may have chosen not to press his request in person.

decisions.choice: found favor in your eyes ... speak in the ears of Pharaoh
decisions.reason: Polite formulas: "if you are willing" and "tell Pharaoh".

decisions.choice: If you are willing to help me
alternatives: If I have found favor in your eyes
decisions.reason: Readable explains the polite formula.

records.source: אָבִ֞י הִשְׁבִּיעַ֣נִי לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ מֵת֒ בְּקִבְרִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן שָׁ֖מָּה תִּקְבְּרֵ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶֽעֱלֶה־נָּ֛א וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה אֶת־אָבִ֖י וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃
records.gloss: My father made me swear, saying, look, I [am] about to die; in my grave which I dug for myself in [the] land of Canaan, there you will bury me. And now, let me go up, please, that I may bury my father, and I will return.
pieces: 'My father bound me by an oath, saying, "I am about to die. Bury me in the grave I prepared for myself in the land of Canaan." So now, please let me travel up there to bury my father; afterward I will return.'"

L.5: 'My father made me swear, saying, "Look, I am about to die; in my grave which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me." So now, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.'"

R.5: 'My father made me promise to bury him in the grave he had prepared for himself in the land of Canaan, because he was about to die. Please let me go there and bury my father. Then I will come back.'"

decisions.reason: Karah usually means to dig. A verb with the same letters means to buy (Deuteronomy 2:6; Hosea 3:2), which would fit the purchase of the cave by Abraham. Jacob may have prepared a place for himself in the family cave.
Jacob made Joseph swear with his hand under his thigh not to bury him in Egypt (47:29-31). Joseph tells Pharaoh of the oath, and of his promise to return, so that Pharaoh can grant the request.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֑ה עֲלֵ֛ה וּקְבֹ֥ר אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh, go up and bury your father, just as he made you swear.
pieces: "Go up and bury your father," Pharaoh replied, "as you swore to him you would."

L.6: And Pharaoh said, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear."

R.6: Pharaoh told him, "You may go. Bury your father, just as you promised him you would."

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַל יוֹסֵ֖ף לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וַיַּֽעֲל֨וּ אִתּ֜וֹ כָּל־עַבְדֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בֵית֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל זִקְנֵ֥י אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And went up Joseph to bury his father, and went up with him all [the] servants of Pharaoh, [the] elders of his house, and all [the] elders of [the] land of Egypt,
pieces: Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all Pharaoh's officials, the senior men of his household and every leading man in Egypt,

L.7: So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

R.7: Joseph set out to bury his father. All of Pharaoh's officials went with him. The leaders of Pharaoh's palace and all the leaders of Egypt went too.

decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court officials; "elders" are senior men with authority, at court and in the land. Egypt honors Jacob with a state funeral.
Pharaoh's "servants" are his courtiers, so Balanced and Readable say "officials".

records.source: וְכֹל֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאֶחָ֖יו וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו רַ֗ק טַפָּם֙ וְצֹאנָ֣ם וּבְקָרָ֔ם עָזְב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: and all [the] house of Joseph, and his brothers, and [the] house of his father. Only their little ones and their flocks and their herds they left in [the] land of Goshen.
pieces: and also Joseph's whole household, his brothers, and the household of his father. They left nothing in the land of Goshen but their little ones, their flocks and their herds.

L.8: and all the household of Joseph, and his brothers, and his father's household. Only their little ones and their flocks and their herds they left in the land of Goshen.

R.8: All of Joseph's family went, and his brothers, and everyone in his father's family. They left only their little children and their sheep, goats and cattle in Goshen.

decisions.choice: the little ones and the flocks left behind
decisions.reason: Leaving children and flocks in Goshen made sure the family would come back. In Exodus, Pharaoh tries to keep the little ones and the flocks in Egypt to stop Israel leaving for good (Exodus 10:9-11, 24-26).

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַל עִמּ֔וֹ גַּם־רֶ֖כֶב גַּם־פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And went up with him both chariots and horsemen, and was the company very great.
pieces: Chariots and riders went up with him as well, so that the camp was very large indeed.

L.9: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen, and the company was very great.

R.9: Chariots and horsemen went too, so there was a very big crowd of people.

decisions.choice: chariots and horsemen: a royal escort
decisions.reason: Egypt's chariot force accompanied the funeral as an honor guard. The same words describe the army that pursued Israel at the sea (Exodus 14:9).
Machaneh is a camp or a large group on the move, as an army is.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַד־גֹּ֣רֶן הָאָטָ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּ֨סְפְּדוּ־שָׁ֔ם מִסְפֵּ֛ד גָּד֥וֹל וְכָבֵ֖ד מְאֹ֑ד וַיַּ֧עַשׂ לְאָבִ֛יו אֵ֖בֶל שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they came to [the] threshing floor of Atad, which [is] beyond the Jordan, and they lamented there a lament great and very heavy; and he made for his father a mourning of seven days.
pieces: They came to Atad's threshing floor, beyond the Jordan, and there they wailed long and bitterly; Joseph held seven days of mourning for his father.

L.10: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lamented there with a very great and heavy lamentation; and he made a mourning for his father of seven days.

R.10: They came to the threshing floor of Atad, on the other side of the Jordan River. There they cried loudly and mourned deeply. Joseph mourned for his father for seven days.

decisions.reason: Atad means a thornbush. The place is not known today.

From the land of Canaan, "beyond the Jordan" usually means east of the river. If so, the procession went around the Dead Sea, the way Israel would later come into the land. The phrase can depend on where the speaker stands, so the exact place is uncertain.
Seven days was the time of mourning at a burial (1 Samuel 31:13).
Balanced and Readable name Joseph as the one who held the mourning.

records.source: וַיַּ֡רְא יוֹשֵׁב֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֜י אֶת־הָאֵ֗בֶל בְּגֹ֨רֶן֙ הָֽאָטָ֔ד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵֽבֶל־כָּבֵ֥ד זֶ֖ה לְמִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ אָבֵ֣ל מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] inhabitant[s] of the land, the Canaanite[s], the mourning at [the] threshing floor of Atad, and they said, a heavy mourning this [is] for Egypt; therefore one called its name Abel-mizraim, which [is] beyond the Jordan.
pieces: The people of the land, the Canaanites, watched the mourning at Atad's threshing floor and said, "How bitterly the Egyptians are mourning!" So the place was given the name Abel-mizraim; it lies beyond the Jordan.

L.11: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a heavy mourning for the Egyptians." Therefore its name was called Abel-mizraim; it is beyond the Jordan.

R.11: The Canaanites living in that land watched the mourning at Atad's threshing floor. They said, "The Egyptians are very sad. Look how they mourn!" So that place on the other side of the Jordan River got the name Abel-mizraim, which means "mourning of Egypt."

decisions.choice: Abel-mizraim: "mourning of Egypt", a play on sound
decisions.reason: Evel means mourning; abel, which sounds almost the same, means a meadow and is common in place names. The Canaanites took Joseph's company for Egyptians, and the place was named for the grief they saw.
Readable explains the name, since the play on words is lost in English.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בָנָ֖יו ל֑וֹ כֵּ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And did his sons for him thus, just as he had commanded them.
pieces: So Jacob's sons carried out for him exactly what he had instructed them.

L.12: And his sons did for him just as he had commanded them.

R.12: Jacob's sons followed their father's orders.

decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, since Joseph has been the subject of the last verses.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ בָנָיו֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בִּמְעָרַ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָה֩ אַבְרָהָ֨ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה לַאֲחֻזַּת־קֶ֗בֶר מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And carried him his sons to [the] land of Canaan, and they buried him in [the] cave of [the] field of Machpelah, which bought Abraham with the field as a possession of a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.
pieces: They bore him to the land of Canaan and laid him in the cave of the Machpelah field, east of Mamre, the field that Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite to own as a burial site.

L.13: And his sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought with the field as a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

R.13: They took their father's body to Canaan. There they buried him in the cave at Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite. Abraham bought it so his family would have a place to bury their dead.

decisions.choice: Jacob buried in the promised land
decisions.reason: Jacob goes home to the land God promised before his descendants do; his burial in Canaan is a pledge that they will follow (verse 24).

records.source: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יוֹסֵ֤ף מִצְרַ֨יְמָה֙ ה֣וּא וְאֶחָ֔יו וְכָל־הָעֹלִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֑יו אַחֲרֵ֖י קָבְר֥וֹ אֶת־אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And returned Joseph to Egypt, he and his brothers and all those who had gone up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
pieces: Once his father was buried, Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.

L.14: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

R.14: When the burial was over, Joseph went home to Egypt. His brothers went back with him, and so did everyone else who had come along.

decisions.reason: The family returns to Egypt, as Joseph promised Pharaoh. The time for them to leave has not yet come (15:13-16).

records.source: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֲחֵֽי־יוֹסֵף֙ כִּי־מֵ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ ל֥וּ יִשְׂטְמֵ֖נוּ יוֹסֵ֑ף וְהָשֵׁ֤ב יָשִׁיב֙ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּמַ֖לְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] brothers of Joseph that had died their father, and they said, if bears a grudge [against] us Joseph, and surely repays to us all the evil which we dealt out to him.
pieces: With their father dead, Joseph's brothers began to worry. "Joseph may be nursing a grudge against us," they said, "and he may pay us back in full for all the harm we did him."

L.15: And when Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "What if Joseph bears a grudge against us and repays us in full for all the evil that we did to him?"

R.15: Their father had died, and Joseph's brothers became frightened. They said, "Maybe Joseph still hates us. He might get even with us for all the evil things we did to him."

decisions.choice: bears a grudge: the fear of a brother's revenge
decisions.reason: The same verb, satam, described Esau's grudge against Jacob, when Esau planned to kill him once their father had died (27:41). The brothers fear that Joseph has only been waiting for Jacob's death.

decisions.choice: repays us in full: an emphatic verb
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled in Hebrew for emphasis: pay back completely.
Lu here introduces a possibility the brothers dread.
Balanced and Readable name the fear that the brothers' words show.

records.source: וַיְצַוּ֕וּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֣יךָ צִוָּ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹת֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And they sent a command to Joseph, saying, your father commanded before his death, saying,
pieces: So they had someone take a message to Joseph: "Your father, before he died, gave this order:

L.16: And they sent word to Joseph, saying, "Your father commanded before his death, saying,

R.16: So they sent someone to Joseph with this message: "Your father gave us an order while he was still alive. He said,

decisions.choice: they sent word: they sent a message by others
decisions.reason: The verb is "commanded"; here it means they had a message carried to Joseph, perhaps by one of them.
Genesis does not record Jacob giving this instruction. He may have said it, or the brothers may have used their father's name to protect themselves.

records.source: כֹּֽה־תֹאמְר֣וּ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף אָ֣נָּ֡א שָׂ֣א נָ֠א פֶּ֣שַׁע אַחֶ֤יךָ וְחַטָּאתָם֙ כִּי־רָעָ֣ה גְמָל֔וּךָ וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א נָ֔א לְפֶ֥שַׁע עַבְדֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ יוֹסֵ֖ף בְּדַבְּרָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Thus you will say to Joseph, please, forgive, please, [the] transgression of your brothers and their sin, for evil they dealt out to you. And now, forgive, please, [the] transgression of [the] servants of [the] God of your father. And wept Joseph when they spoke to him.
pieces: 'Say this to Joseph: "I beg you, forgive your brothers' crime and their sin, the wrong they did to you."' So now, please forgive the crime of the servants of your father's God." At their words Joseph wept.

L.17: 'Thus you shall say to Joseph: "Please, forgive, please, the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they did evil to you."' And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

R.17: 'Tell Joseph: "Please forgive your brothers for the evil and the wrong they did to you."' So now, please forgive us. We serve the God your father served." These words made Joseph cry.

decisions.reason: Pesha is a breach of trust, a wrong against someone with a rightful claim on you; chattat is missing the mark. Together they cover the whole wrong done to Joseph.

decisions.choice: servants of the God of your father: an appeal to shared faith
decisions.reason: The brothers ask forgiveness as fellow servants of the same God, the God of Jacob.
The text does not say why. Joseph may have been grieved that after seventeen years his brothers still feared him, or moved by their confession.

decisions.choice: So now, please forgive us. We serve the God your father served.
alternatives: forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the brothers speak of themselves.
Servants of God are his worshipers, not owned people, so the word is "servants".

records.source: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ גַּם־אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ הִנֶּ֥נּֽוּ לְךָ֖ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And went also his brothers and fell before him and said, here we [are] to you as slaves.
pieces: His brothers then came themselves and fell down before him, saying, "Here we are, your slaves."

L.18: And his brothers also went and fell down before him and said, "Here we are, your slaves."

R.18: After that his brothers came to him too. They bowed low in front of him and said, "We belong to you as your slaves."

decisions.choice: they fell before him: Joseph's dreams come true
decisions.reason: Joseph had dreamed that his brothers' sheaves bowed to his (37:7-8). Now they offer themselves as his slaves, as they did in 44:16.
Avadim here means slaves: the brothers offer Joseph their freedom.
"Slaves" at every level: the brothers offer Joseph their freedom (m2), as in 44:16, so the style guide keeps the word.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ כִּ֛י הֲתַ֥חַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said to them Joseph, do not fear, for in [the] place of God [am] I?
pieces: Joseph answered them, "Have no fear. Do I stand in the place of God?

L.19: But Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid, for am I in the place of God?

R.19: Joseph told them, "You do not need to be afraid. I cannot take the place of God.

decisions.choice: am I in the place of God?: judgment belongs to God
decisions.reason: Joseph refuses to sit in judgment on his brothers or to take revenge, which is God's right (Deuteronomy 32:35). Jacob had used the same words to Rachel (30:2).

decisions.choice: I cannot take the place of God
alternatives: Am I in the place of God?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects the answer "no", into a statement.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֕ם חֲשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָלַ֖י רָעָ֑ה אֱלֹהִים֙ חֲשָׁבָ֣הּ לְטֹבָ֔ה לְמַ֗עַן עֲשֹׂ֛ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֥ת עַם־רָֽב׃
records.gloss: And you, you planned against me evil; God planned it for good, in order to do as this day, to keep alive a people numerous.
pieces: Evil was what you planned against me; good was what God planned by it, so as to bring about what you see today: the lives of a great many people saved.

L.20: As for you, you planned evil against me; God planned it for good, in order to do as [it is] this day, to keep many people alive.

R.20: You planned to hurt me. But God planned to use it for good. He did it so that many people could stay alive, as you can see today.

decisions.choice: you planned ... God planned: one deed, two purposes
decisions.reason: The same verb, chashav, is used of the brothers and of God. The brothers meant harm; God, working through the same events, meant good. Joseph said this when he first made himself known (45:5-8).
The famine would have destroyed Egypt, the nations around it and Jacob's family; Joseph's place in Egypt preserved them all (41:57; 45:7).
Literal supplies the verb Hebrew leaves out.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תִּירָ֔אוּ אָנֹכִ֛י אֲכַלְכֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־טַפְּכֶ֑ם וַיְנַחֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־לִבָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And now, do not fear; I will provide for you and your little ones. And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.
pieces: So there is no need to fear. I will see that you and your little ones have what you need." He comforted them, speaking kindly to them.

L.21: So now, do not be afraid; I will provide for you and your little ones." And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.

R.21: So stop being afraid. I will make sure you and your children have food and everything you need." Joseph comforted them with kind words.

decisions.choice: provide for: supply food and needs
decisions.reason: Kul is the verb Joseph used when he promised to feed his family through the famine (45:11; 47:12). The promise continues after Jacob's death.

decisions.choice: spoke to their heart: spoke kindly
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak tenderly and reassuringly (34:3; Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: speaking kindly to them / with kind words
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom.

records.source: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יוֹסֵף֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם ה֖וּא וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו וַיְחִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And lived Joseph in Egypt, he and [the] house of his father; and lived Joseph 110 years.
pieces: Joseph went on living in Egypt together with his father's household, and he reached the age of 110.

L.22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his father's household; and Joseph lived 110 years.

R.22: Joseph and all his father's family stayed in Egypt. Joseph lived a long life, 110 years in all.

decisions.reason: In Egyptian texts 110 years was the ideal length of a life. Joshua, who led Israel into the land, also died at 110 (Joshua 24:29).

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא יוֹסֵף֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּנֵ֖י שִׁלֵּשִׁ֑ים גַּ֗ם בְּנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יֻלְּד֖וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵּ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And saw Joseph of Ephraim sons of [the] third [generation]; also [the] sons of Machir, [the] son of Manasseh, were born on [the] knees of Joseph.
pieces: Joseph saw Ephraim's descendants to the third generation; the children of Machir, Manasseh's son, were also received on Joseph's knees at their birth.

L.23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children of the third [generation]; also the children of Machir the son of Manasseh were born on Joseph's knees.

R.23: Joseph lived to see Ephraim's family down to the third generation. When the children of Manasseh's son Machir were born, Joseph took them on his knees as his own.

decisions.reason: The word means the third generation, counted either from Ephraim (his grandchildren) or from Joseph (his great-grandchildren). Either way Joseph saw a long line of descendants, a sign of blessing (Psalm 128:6).

decisions.choice: born on Joseph's knees: accepted into the family
decisions.reason: Placing a newborn on one's knees was a sign of claiming the child (30:3; 48:12). Joseph receives Machir's children as his own.

decisions.choice: Machir: a leading clan of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Machir's descendants became a powerful part of the tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 32:39-40; Judges 5:14).

decisions.choice: Joseph took them on his knees as his own
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־אֶחָ֔יו אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים פָּקֹ֧ד יִפְקֹ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֗ם וְהֶעֱלָ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֛ע לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers, I [am] about to die, and God will surely visit you, and he will bring you up from this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
pieces: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will not fail to come and help you; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lead you up out of this land to the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob."

L.24: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will surely visit you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring you up from this land to the land which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."

R.24: Joseph said to his brothers, "My life is almost over. But God will certainly come to help you. He will lead you out of this land and take you to the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised with an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."

decisions.choice: God will surely visit you: come to help
decisions.reason: Paqad is to attend to someone, to come and act for them, as God "visited" Sarah (21:1). The doubled verb makes it certain. When Moses comes, God uses the same words: "I have surely visited you" (Exodus 3:16; 4:31).

decisions.choice: the land he swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The first time the three names stand together in the Bible: God's oath to each of them (22:16-17; 26:3; 28:13) now rests on all their descendants.
"Brothers" may include the wider family of Israel, since some of Joseph's brothers may have died before him.
The pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting; at the start of a Readable sentence plain "He" is used.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִתֶ֥ם אֶת־עַצְמֹתַ֖י מִזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And made swear Joseph [the] sons of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and you will bring up my bones from here.
pieces: Joseph then put the sons of Israel under oath: "God will not fail to come and help you, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, you are to take my bones up with you from here."

L.25: And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here."

R.25: Joseph made the Israelites promise him, "God is sure to come and help you. When that happens, you must take my bones with you when you leave this place."

decisions.choice: carry up my bones: Joseph's faith in the promise
decisions.reason: Joseph wanted to be buried in the promised land, like his father. Moses took Joseph's bones with him out of Egypt (Exodus 13:19), and they were buried at Shechem (Joshua 24:32). Hebrews 11:22 counts this as an act of faith.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: Jacob's family, the future Israelites
decisions.reason: The phrase means Jacob's sons and their families, and it becomes the usual name of the people in Exodus.

decisions.choice: when he does / When that happens
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the link between God's coming and the carrying up of the bones explicit.

records.source: וַיָּ֣מָת יוֹסֵ֔ף בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִ֑ים וַיַּחַנְט֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַיִּ֥ישֶׂם בָּאָר֖וֹן בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And died Joseph, a son of 110 years; and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
pieces: Joseph died at 110 years of age. He was embalmed and put in a coffin in Egypt.

L.26: And Joseph died, 110 years old; and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

R.26: Joseph died when he was 110 years old. They embalmed his body and put it in a coffin in Egypt.

decisions.choice: a son of 110 years: 110 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being a "son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: a coffin in Egypt: Genesis ends waiting
decisions.reason: The book that began with God creating life ends with a coffin in Egypt. But the coffin is waiting to be carried out (verse 25), and the story continues in Exodus. Aron, coffin, is also the word for the ark of the covenant.
